paper_metadata.title: Development and thermal stability of Cr10Mo25Ta25Ti15V25 refractory high entropy alloys

evidence.quote: In this study, a new CrMoTaTiV RHEA system has been designed using CALPHAD modeling and thermophysical parameter optimization, and produced by vacuum arc melting.

Refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs) are promising materials for extreme environment applications, such as high-temperatures (> 1000 °C), corrosion and irradiation. In this study, a new CrMoTaTiV RHEA system has been designed using CALPHAD modeling and thermophysical parameter optimization, and produced by vacuum arc melting.

process_steps.input_state: mixed granules of Cr, Mo, Ta, Ti, V

evidence.quote: Compact Arc Melter MAM-1 was used to manufacture the alloy. Granules of Cr (99.9 wt%), Mo (99.95 wt%), Ta (99.9 wt%), Ti (99.99 wt%) and V (99.7 wt%) elements were mixed and placed in the arc melter. Before each melting stage, the chamber was vacuumed and flushed with Ar gas at least three times. Produced beads were flipped and remelted at least five times for full mixing and melting of the elements.

Fig. 2b shows that Cr10Mo25Ta25Ti15V25 alloy has a single-phase BCC structure, as opposed to the equilibrium CALPHAD calculations. Since VAM samples are subjected to rapid cooling, sluggish diffusion mechanism does not allow microstructure to show any solid-state phase transformation. Thus, instead of the formation of other BCC and HCP phases, high-temperature phase becomes supersaturated and remains as a single phase at room temperature. The lattice parameter of this phase is measured as 3.18 Å.

attributes.composition: Ti-rich with some carbon, Ti-C solid solution

evidence.quote: The diffraction spots encircled by red color belong to BCC RHEA while planes labeled in white color belong to Ti-rich second phase having FCC crystal structure along [110] zone axis. The lattice parameter of this phase has been calculated as 4.42 Å. High annular angular dark field (HAADF) image in Fig. 7b clearly shows the concentration difference in bright and dark grains (and needle-like features) in Fig. 7a. Darker grains have smaller weights compared to the background RHEA composition. EDX analysis also indicated that these regions are rich in titanium with some carbon, which is the solid solution of Ti-C having FCC crystal structure.
After the VAM production, microstructure is observed to be dendritic as a result of rapid cooling. Clearly, the dendrite size becomes finer towards outer regions as indicated by an arrow in Fig. 2a.

attributes.composition: enriched with Ti, V, Cr and depleted with Ta and Mo

evidence.quote: Fig. 3a shows the elemental distribution in Cr10Mo25Ta25Ti15V25 alloy. There is some V, Ti and Cr segregation while Ta and Mo depletion occurs at the interdendritic regions.

Similar to the EBSD observations, TEM analyses indicate the formation of some nano-crystalline grains and cells within large dendrites. Fig. 5a shows a region having mostly the nanocrystals with high angle grain boundaries as the diffraction contrast infers.
Fig. 6a and b show dislocation tangles besides linear dislocations. Fig. 6c shows linearly aligned dislocation loop structures, similar to the ones observed in EBSD analyses (Fig. 4d).
High strength and ductility of this alloy at the temperatures up to 1000 °C compared to the other RHEA systems have been attributed to its unique microstructure.
